For the fourth year in a row, AIG has been recognized as one of TIME’s[“Best Companies for Future Leaders.”](https://time.com/article/2026/11/19/best-companies-for-future-leaders-2027/)


At AIG, our Learn-It-All culture encourages curiosity, collaboration and new ideas. Through leadership development and new challenges, we empower our colleagues to strengthen critical skills and expand their expertise.


### “We’re proud of this recognition and what it represents as part of our commitment to helping our colleagues build meaningful careers at AIG,” says[Kelly Lafnitzegger](https://www.aig.com/home/about/leadership-and-governance/kelly-lafnitzegger) , AIG's Executive Vice President and Chief Human Resources Officer. “From emerging talent to experienced professionals and leaders, our focus is on giving colleagues the tools and experiences to grow at every stage.”


Statista examined the professional and educational backgrounds of about 5,900 influential U.S.-based leaders, including CEOs of leading public and private companies and leaders in politics and government, encompassing about 28,000 positions. The recognition went to 300 organizations, including 175 companies and 125 colleges. Each organization’s Leadership Index reflects the number of leaders connected to it through employment or education. Results are adjusted for company headcount or college enrollment to allow for more balanced comparisons among organizations of different sizes.
